title: Rice (Oryza sativa) Crop Profile & Cultivation Guide
seed_rate: 20 - 25 kg/acre for transplanted rice; 8 - 10 kg/acre for SRD
fertilizer_recommendation: N:P:K = 100:50:50 kg/hectare (Apply N in 3 split doses: basal, tillering, panicle initiation)
harvest_period: Harvest when 80-85% of grains turn straw-golden yellow and grain moisture drops to 20%.
content: Rice is the primary staple food crop in India grown predominantly during the Kharif season. It thrives in heavy clay or alluvial soils capable of holding standing water. Key stages include nursery bed preparation, transplanting 21-25 day old seedlings, maintaining 2-5cm water level during tillering, and applying split doses of Nitrogen and Zinc Sulphate.
source: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) & Directorate of Rice Research

title: Maize (Zea mays) Crop Profile & Cultivation Guide
suitable_soil: Well-drained Fertile Loamy, Alluvial, or Black Soil (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
fertilizer_recommendation: N:P:K = 120:60:40 kg/hectare (Split Nitrogen at basal, knee-high stage, and tasseling stage)
harvest_period: Harvest when cob husk leaves dry up and turn pale brown and grain moisture is around 20%.
content: Maize (Corn) is a versatile cereal crop grown for food, fodder, and industrial bio-products. Requires well-drained fertile loamy soils. Susceptible to waterlogging during early seedling stages. Critical growth stages needing irrigation are knee-high stage, tasseling, silking, and grain filling.
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR)

title: Chickpea / Gram (Cicer arietinum) Cultivation Guide
suitable_soil: Well-drained Black Soil, Sandy Loam, Clay Loam (pH 6.0 - 8.0)
seed_rate: 30 - 35 kg/acre for Desi; 40 - 45 kg/acre for Kabuli
fertilizer_recommendation: N:P:K = 20:50:20 kg/hectare + Rhizobium inoculation + 20 kg Sulphur/ha
harvest_period: Harvest when leaves turn yellow and pods dry up, producing a rattling sound when shaken.
content: Chickpea (Chana) is the premier pulse crop of India grown during the cool Rabi season. It fixes atmospheric nitrogen in soil through root nodules. Highly sensitive to waterlogging and high humidity at flowering. Requires 1-2 light irrigations at pre-flowering and pod-development stages.
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR)

title: Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) Cultivation Guide
fertilizer_recommendation: N:P:K = 120:60:60 kg/hectare (Apply N in 3 splits at 30, 60, and 90 days post sowing)
harvest_period: Harvest in multiple pickings as bolls burst open fully exposing dry white cotton lint.
content: Cotton is the leading commercial cash fiber crop in India. It grows best in deep moisture-retentive black clay soils. Requires 180 frost-free days and bright sunshine during boll maturation. Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes rank vegetative growth.
source: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR)

title: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) Cultivation Guide
suitable_soil: Fertile Alluvial Soil, Clay Loam, Loamy Soil (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
seed_rate: 40 - 45 kg/acre for normal sowing; 50 kg/acre for late sowing
fertilizer_recommendation: N:P:K = 120:60:40 kg/hectare (Apply 50% N + 100% P & K as basal; 50% N at Crown Root Initiation)
harvest_period: Harvest when straw turns golden yellow, grains feel hard and moisture drops below 14%.
content: Wheat is the dominant winter cereal crop in Northern and Central India. Crown Root Initiation (CRI stage at 21 days) is the most critical irrigation stage. Proper cold temperature during tillering promotes higher yield.
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR)

title: Sugarcane (Saccharum officinarum) Cultivation Guide
suitable_soil: Deep Alluvial, Loamy, and Heavy Black Soils (pH 6.5 - 8.0)
fertilizer_recommendation: N:P:K = 250:115:115 kg/hectare (Split Nitrogen applications over vegetative growth phase)
harvest_period: Harvest when sucrose content reaches 16-18% and brix reading exceeds 18.
content: Sugarcane is a long-duration commercial sugar crop. It requires warm, humid climate, high water availability, and deep rich loamy or black soils. Earthing-up and trash mulching help conserve soil moisture and prevent lodging.

title: Groundnut / Peanut (Arachis hypogaea) Cultivation Guide
suitable_soil: Well-drained Sandy Loam, Red Loam, Light Clay Loam (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
fertilizer_recommendation: N:P:K = 20:40:40 kg/ha + 200 kg Gypsum/ha at flowering (peg initiation)
harvest_period: Harvest when leaves turn yellow, inner pod shell turns dark brown, and kernel skin becomes pink.
content: Groundnut (Peanut) is an important oilseed and food legume crop. Requires friable loose sandy loam soil allowing easy peg penetration into the soil for pod formation. Apply Gypsum at 45 days (flowering/pegging) to supply Calcium and Sulphur essential for pod filling.

title: Mustard / Rapeseed (Brassica juncea) Cultivation Guide
suitable_soil: Sandy Loam to Heavy Loam Soils (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
harvest_period: Harvest when 75% of pods turn yellowish-golden to prevent pod shattering.
content: Mustard is a major winter oilseed crop in India. It thrives under cool temperatures and moderate moisture. Highly responsive to Sulphur application which increases seed oil concentration.

title: Mango (Mangifera indica) Cultivation Guide
suitable_soil: Deep, well-drained Alluvial or Red Loamy Soil (pH 5.5 - 7.5)
water_requirement: Moderate (Requires dry spell during winter for flowering initiation)
seed_rate: Grafted saplings planted at 10m x 10m spacing (100 trees/ha)
fertilizer_recommendation: 1000g N, 500g P2O5, 1000g K2O per bearing tree per year applied post-harvest.
harvest_period: Harvest when fruits reach full size and shoulder maturity (specific gravity 1.01-1.02).
content: Mango is the King of Fruits in India. Thrives in tropical to sub-tropical climates with a distinct dry period prior to flowering. Avoid nitrogen fertilizer during flowering to prevent flower drop.
source: ICAR - Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (CISH)

title: Banana (Musa acuminata) Cultivation Guide
seed_rate: Tissue culture plantlets planted at 1.8m x 1.8m (3000 plants/ha)
fertilizer_recommendation: N:P:K = 200:50:300 grams per plant in 4-6 split doses
harvest_period: Harvest when fruit angles become rounded and color changes from dark green to light green.
content: Banana is a fast-growing, heavy feeding fruit crop. Requires warm humid climate, abundant water, and high potassium fertilization. Drip irrigation and fertigation produce maximum bunch weight.
source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB)
